## What is still open

- Maya is waiting on your number before she approves #247: how many Orbitly events were dropped since #240. She needs it for Thursday's call with Orbitly. Your answer is ~1.18M legitimate events dropped (4,352 genuine replays excluded), ≈8.1% of their iOS volume. Zest lost 3,812 events the same way [1][2].
- After #247 is merged and deployed, run the replay from landing for Orbitly (from 2026-11-13 09:40 UTC, about 40 min) and for Zest. Then check that `ingest_dedupe_dropped_total{project="prj_0rb1"}` stays near zero. Run it only after the deploy, or the old key drops the events again [1].
- Before Friday's incident review (20/11), you owe an alert for when the dead-letter queue goes above 1,000 messages [7].
- The note asking the iOS team to restore UUIDs for `event_id` in kestrel-ios 3.2.1 is drafted but not yet sent [1].

## What changed

- Maya says the logic of #247 looks right and she will approve once CI is green [2].
- Noa published the final 12/11 postmortem and will present it on Friday [3].

## What you did

- You traced Orbitly's ~8% iOS funnel drop to our own SDK 3.2.0, whose per-session `event_id` collided under #240's dedupe. You opened #247, which keys on project, device and event_id [1][2].
